scenario.description: A fund operations director must approve the cash redemption plan for several investors and finalize the distribution amount, priority payment, reserve, and tax controls, with input from fund accounting, investor relations, and tax.

shared_context.S1: The fund has $12,000,000 of cash and has received redemption requests totaling $10,000,000.
shared_context.S2: The fund's net asset value is $20,000,000, and the standard practice is to pay approved redemptions in cash within 30 days when liquidity permits.
shared_context.S3: The redemption requests were received on 2026-10-21.
shared_context.S4: Nadia makes the binding decision on the redemption plan.
shared_context.S5: The fund's standard pre-distribution sign-off includes a round-robin review by fund accounting, investor relations, and tax before Nadia finalizes the plan.

PF1.text: While closing the October cash forecast this morning, Elliot confirmed that the fund must retain $3,000,000 of operating liquidity and reserve $2,000,000 for a capital call due in 14 days; these amounts have not yet been circulated in the redemption file.

PF2.text: Maya found a signed investor side letter while reviewing the relationship file this week: Investor Redwood must receive exactly $3,000,000 in cash from this redemption cycle no later than 2026-11-20, although the side letter has not been added to the distribution worksheet.

PF3.text: Jonas confirmed in a tax memo received this morning that $600,000 must remain reserved for withholding and related tax remittances from this redemption cycle; he has not yet updated the tax checklist.

acceptance_conditions: The total cash distribution must be exactly $6,400,000.
The fund must retain exactly $5,600,000 in cash after the distribution.
Investor Redwood must receive exactly $3,000,000 from the distribution.
The payment date must be exactly 2026-11-20.
The plan must include a $2,000,000 capital-call reserve commitment.
The plan must include a $600,000 tax-withholding reserve commitment.

content_checks.C5: any(('capital call' in c['target']) or ('capital call' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: any(('withholding' in c['target']) or ('withholding' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: Without PF1, the shared $12,000,000 cash balance supports a generic larger distribution; PF1 establishes the exact $5,000,000 operating and capital-call holdback, changing total_cash_distribution_usd to $7,000,000 before the tax reserve and requiring the $2,000,000 capital-call commitment.
Without PF2, the redemption requests provide no basis for paying Investor Redwood exactly $3,000,000 or setting payment_date to 2026-11-20.

Without PF3, the required cash holdback is only $5,000,000, but PF3 adds exactly $600,000, changing total_cash_distribution_usd to $6,400,000 and cash_reserve_usd to $5,600,000 while requiring the tax-withholding commitment.
